evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Treat data quality as non-negotiable: investigate anomalies, follow up persistently with data engineers and source system owners to resolve root causes rather than apply patches
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: The JD repeatedly emphasizes correctness, root-cause resolution over workarounds, testing, and governance, with no velocity/speed language present.
evidence.domain_risk: Experience in fintech, investment, or financial services domains
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Ajaib is an investment platform and fintech domain familiarity is explicitly named as a nice-to-have, but it's not framed with regulatory/compliance override language, keeping this at moderate rather than high.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A named 'Analytics & Data Engineering team' with existing governance frameworks, taxonomy tags, and CI/CD for dbt already in place indicates a growing, established function rather than a from-zero build.
evidence.jd_authorship: Design, build, and maintain dbt models on BigQuery, following modular and tested transformation patterns (staging → intermediate → marts)
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities name precise methodology (staging→intermediate→marts, Kimball dimensional modeling, taxonomy tags, CDC/streaming ingestion) that shows exactly what the role does day to day, written by someone close to the work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Partner with analysts, PMs, and business stakeholders to translate requirements into well-modeled datasets and clear metric definitions
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role centers on the transformation/modeling layer serving internal analysts and data consumers rather than one specific commercial, product, or finance function.
evidence.autonomy_level: Proactively identify gaps and propose new AE initiatives — better testing frameworks, semantic layers, metric stores, internal tooling, automation — when current work feels routine.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role combines self-directed initiative and ownership language (strategic) with scoped execution duties like building assigned dbt models and mentoring (execution), making this mixed.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: ML use cases are mentioned as downstream consumers of the data the candidate builds, but no AI coding tool usage or AI-specific infrastructure building is asked of the candidate.
evidence.testing_framing: Treat data quality as non-negotiable: investigate anomalies, follow up persistently with data engineers and source system owners to resolve root causes rather than apply patches, and advocate for fixes upstream when needed
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data quality is framed as an owned, non-negotiable responsibility with explicit ownership verbs (investigate, advocate, resolve), not just a tool in a skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: data correctness is something worth fighting for, and we want someone who pushes back when the numbers don't add up
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Reliability and correctness are a recurring, strongly worded concern throughout responsibilities, but the framing is about craft/ownership rather than regulatory or stakeholder-trust fear specifically, placing this at moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Proactively identify gaps and propose new AE initiatives — better testing frameworks, semantic layers, metric stores, internal tooling, automation
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The role both maintains existing dbt models/pipelines (fix/scale) and is expected to propose and build new initiatives (greenfield), making this mixed.
evidence.loss_aversion: data correctness is something worth fighting for, and we want someone who pushes back when the numbers don't add up — reflects a craft/ownership-driven reliability concern rather than a dominant compliance risk register.
